content.comment_body: Hello everyone. Here is a program I created for bidirectional motor control. I want to be able to pause the motor sequence at any point using a remaining cursor key, but I haven’t figured out how to implement this. Additionally, I’d like to add a maximum operation time of 2 minutes, with a single adjustable setting for the turn period, preventing users from overrunning the motor. Any assistance would be very helpful, as I am new to working with this type of device and still learning. Password = unlock Thank you.
Does anyone know how to assist with this? I’d really like to understand and master this program. Thank you.
I’d like to help, but I’m unclear about your requirements. Can you provide a detailed explanation of what your circuit is intended to do?

The system controls a motor to rotate left (O1) and right (O2) for a user-defined period, with a delay between each direction change. To ensure the turns always begin from the same position, I use a microswitch input positioned on a cam attached to the motor (I1). Pressing the up cursor starts the program by running the left turn, regardless of the current position, bringing it back to the microswitch. Once the microswitch is triggered, timing begins. Currently, the program requires waiting for the cycle to finish to stop it, which could take hours depending on delays. Also, inconsistent turn times can shift the starting point each cycle if the right turn duration exceeds the left. This can be resolved with only one adjustable turn time and a maximum of 2 minutes. I hope this clarifies my setup, and I appreciate your help.
I worked on this further and managed to solve all issues except one. The remaining challenge is setting a maximum value of 2 minutes for delays or output activations.

I’m still struggling to follow your explanation. I made an attempt for your scenario: - Begin cycle with input 1 - First, turn left until reaching the limit switch on input 3 - Then start the sequence: * Wait time 1 * Rotate right via output 2 * Wait time 2 * Rotate left via output 1 - The sequence then loops back to wait time 1 and continues until power loss or input 2 is pressed. Please configure your cursor keys or other inputs as needed. You can set all timing parameters as you require.

analysis.insight_summary: The main difficulties faced by the user concern setting up a control unit so that motor operations can be paused using a button, and limiting running time with a singular adjustable setting. The user finds it challenging to turn operational requirements into programmable logic, especially as available guidance does not match their beginner level.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a straightforward way to add a pause feature using an input button and assign a single, simple maximum run time for the motor, avoiding complicated programming steps.
